item.title: 伊朗安全负责人威胁邻国反对经济措施和其他中东事态发展
item.description:
The new leader of Iran’s top security body is threatening neighbors against joining new U.S. efforts to squeeze Tehran’s economy. Egypt is trying to revive Iran-U.S. negotiations. And Iraq and Iran say Tehran has helped some ships carrying Iraqi oil to transit theStrait of Hormuz. France and Saudi Arabia are expected to discuss plans to bypass the waterway.
Meanwhile, Israel has carried out strikes in Syria and in Gaza.
Here’s a look at the latest developments in the Iran war and the wider Middle East on Saturday. Full coverage can befound here.
The hard-line new leader of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council threatened Tehran’s neighbors against joining the new U.S. effort to hurt Iran’s economy, and accused the United States of increasing global nuclear insecurity with months of war.
“If (Trump) wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,” he said in an interview with the state broadcaster that aired Saturday.
Mohsen Rezaei was named this month as part of senior appointments widely seen as hardening Tehran’s political and military stance. His interview with IRIB is his most extensive public statement since then.
Rezaei said Iran would target oil-shipping routes out of the Persian Gulf — alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz — if neighbors join what he described as the economic war against Iran. Those neighbors would be considered enemies and “we will target their interests,” he said.
U.S. President Donald Trump in the past week has vowed to increase Iran’s pain by imposing an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation. Iran has lived under sanctions for years.
Rezaei said discussions with Oman, located on the other side of the strait, over management of it were ongoing, and said fees would be imposed. Iran asserted control over what was seen as an international waterway shortly after the U.S. and Israel attacked on Feb. 28.
Rezaei also vowed to make changes to Iran’s diplomacy and bring new capabilities to what he called the next war. He warned the U.S. against sending more military personnel to the region, and said the U.S. had increased nuclear insecurity because countries see that participating in international monitoring efforts, as Iran has done, is no protection against attack.
The top diplomats for Egypt and Iran discussed efforts to bring Tehran and Washington back to the negotiating table to settle the war, Egypt’s foreign ministry said.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Egyptian counterpart Badr Abdelatty also discussed the Iranian-Omani talks, the ministry said.
Araghchi briefed Egypt’s foreign minister about “Iran’s view of ongoing developments, the course of negotiations and their challenges,” the ministry said, without elaborating. Araghchi confirmed the call. Separately, Araghchi said he had a call with Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir,
Residents swim as cargo and commercial vessels are anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026. (Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP)
The governments of Iraq and Iran said Tehran has helped some ships carrying Iraqi oil to transit the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for global oil, natural gas and other supplies, but there were few details.
“There is facilitation for some ships carrying Iraqi oil in the Strait of Hormuz,” Iraqi President Nizar Amidi said in comments published Saturday by the state-run news agency, adding that Iraq doesn’t have a national carrier for transporting oil.
Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency said a number of Iraqi oil tankers have been permitted to transit. It was not clear how many or what Iran might have received in return.
An Israeli drone strike on a vehicle wounded one person on Saturday in the southwestern Syrian village of Beit Jin, according to the Syrian state news agency SANA. Syria’s foreign ministry said several civilians were injured and called the strike a flagrant violation of the country’s sovereignty.
The Israeli military said it targeted a “terrorist who advanced terror attacks in final stages of preparation,” without elaborating. It wasn’t immediately clear if it was the same strike.
Israel has carried out hundreds of airstrikes around Syria after the ouster of former President Bashar Assad in late 2024, mainly destroying army assets to keep them out of the hands of his successors.
In an interview on Friday with Mario Nawfal, a Lebanese-Australian entrepreneur,U.S. Ambassador Tom Barracksaid Israel “still” occupies the Golan Heights in violation of U.N. resolutions.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz on Saturday in a statement called Barrack’s remarks “full of inaccuracies and positions that contradict Trump’s own position.”
Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 war and annexed it in 1981. The U.N. considers the territory occupied Syrian land. But in March 2019, Trump signed a proclamation recognizing Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, reversing decades of U.S. policy.
French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman are expected to discuss plans to develop alternatives routes to the Strait of Hormuz during the Saudi leader’s two-day visit to Paris that starts on Sunday, according to officials in the presidency who weren’t authorized to be publicly named.
Proposals include increasing trade through Omani ports outside of the Persian Gulf, expanding or doubling pipelines in Saudi Arabia and elsewhere, and developing new rail links, the officials said.
France and Saudi Arabia have formed a task force on energy and logistics connections between the Middle East and Europe that is scheduled to meet at the ministerial level Monday. The officials said the work would focus on identifying the most strategic projects, securing financing and establishing roles for French companies.
— AP correspondent Angela Charlton in Paris
The Israeli army demolishes buildings east of Deir al-Balah, central Gaza Strip, Saturday Aug. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Abdel Kareem Hana)
An Israeli strike on the backyard of a house in centralGazakilled one Palestinian and wounded another Saturday, according to health officials at Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital.
Israel’s military said it targeted Sharif al-Hasanat, a Hamas commander who “advanced terror attacks and took part in efforts to restore Hamas’ underground infrastructure.” Days earlier, a U.S. negotiatorreportedly asked Israelto draw down attacks while seeking to make progress on the ceasefire.

item.title: 加拿大和美国之间的贸易战进一步破裂了曾经紧密而持久的联盟
item.description:
TORONTO (AP) — For decades, Canada built much of its prosperity on privileged access to the United States. Now,after the collapse of trade talks, one of the world’s closest and most durable alliances has been fundamentally altered, with both countries facing the risk of afull-scale trade war.
Prime Minister Mark Carney acknowledged the break after last-ditch negotiations failed Friday, saying Canada had recognized that “America has changed” and that the countries would “not return to our old relationship.”
The United States imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods early Saturday. Carney said Canada would retaliate dollar for dollar beginning Sept. 8, targeting sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics.
Carney foreshadowed the shiftat theWorld Economic Forumin Davos in January, declaring that the world was experiencing “a rupture, not a transition” and urging countries such as Canada to reduce their vulnerability to economic coercion by strengthening their economies at home and diversifying abroad.
He said in Ottawa on Saturday that warning had been borne out. He accused the U.S. of using “economic integration as a weapon” and said its “signature was written in pencil.”
“The collapse of the tariff talks points to the fact that the old Canada-U.S. relationship is over and, for many Canadians, it also confirms the perception that Canada can’t trust the Trump administration,” said Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University in Montreal.
The pressure from Republican President Donald Trump has gone well beyond tariffs.
He has questionedCanada’s economic viability, repeatedly talked about making itthe 51st U.S. stateand used trade measures to encourage production to move from Canada to the United States. That has angered many Canadians and fueled a sense of betrayal in a country that had long regarded the U.S. as its closest ally.
Canadian travel to the U.S. remains sharply lower than before the dispute, with July return trips down nearly 29% by car and 27% by air from July 2024, Statistics Canada said.
The failed negotiations underscored how far the relationship had shifted. Canada had been prepared to accept some U.S. tariffs for market access and greater certainty — a break from decades of policy aimed at eliminating trade barriers.
For Canadians accustomed to preferential access under the 1989 Canada-U.S. Free Trade Agreement, NAFTA and its successor, even reduced tariffs would mark a retreat from the old relationship.
The collapse also puts Carney’s approach to Trump to the test.
The prime minister’s “elbows up” posture — hockey shorthand for playing aggressively and refusing to be pushed around — has helped keep him popular at home. His decision to resist U.S. pressure could also resonate abroad with those impressed by his Davos call for countries to resist economic coercion and reduce dependence on great powers.
Provincial and conservative leaders broadly backed Carney. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said “the old status quo is not possible,” while Ontario Premier Doug Ford praised Carney for rejecting what he called a bad deal for the auto, steel and manufacturing sectors.
Ford said Trump “is not to be trusted whatsoever.”
Former Alberta Premier Jason Kenney said Canada was “not cravenly surrendering in the face of constant economic and political aggression.”
Lana Payne, national president of Unifor, Canada’s largest private-sector union, accused Trump of trying to weaken Canada’s industrial base.
“What we have seen from the U.S. administration, or Donald Trump, is this consistent attempt to try and destroy the industrial economy of Canada with tariffs that have been strategically designed to attack us,” Payne said.
Nearly three-quarters of Canada’s goods exports go to the United States. The U.S. economy is roughly 10 times larger than Canada’s, limiting Ottawa’s ability to retaliate dollar for dollar without inflicting disproportionate damage at home.
Royal Bank of Canada economists estimate the tariffs directly affect about 0.4% of Canada’s GDP because they cover only about 5% of Canadian exports to the U.S. The damage could grow if retaliation broadens, more sectors are targeted or the dispute curbs investment and disrupts supply chains.
Carney himself acknowledged the cost of retaliation, saying the Canadian measures would “raise costs and reduce choice for Canadians.” He said his government would announce additional assistance for affected businesses and workers.
Béland said the countries were witnessing “the beginning of a full-scale trade war,” though he cautioned that the situation could change rapidly.
Carney said Canada supplies 99% of U.S. natural gas imports, 85% of its electricity imports and 60% of its crude oil imports. Trump has focused much of his pressure on autos, steel and aluminum, fueling resentment among Canadians who see the push as an effort to hollow out key industries.
Goldy Hyder, president and CEO of the Business Council of Canada, said businesses still view the U.S. as Canada’s most important trading partner but increasingly see the shift as lasting beyond Trump.
“There is a new trade and investment model, one that could well be kept in place by future U.S. administrations whether Democrat or Republican,” Hyder said.
The breakdown adds urgency to Carney’s push to diversify beyond the United States. He has traveled abroad seeking investment and new trade ties, aiming to attract $1 trillion Canadian (US$730 billion) by 2030 and double non-U.S. investment over the next decade. Canada has signed more than 20 trade and security agreements across five continents in the past year.
That made Washington’s effort to restrict Canada’s ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries particularly significant.
In July, Ottawa and Alberta advanced plans for a new Pacific Coast oil pipeline to give Canadian crude greater access to Asian markets and reduce reliance on U.S. buyers.
The immediate question is how long the latest tariff confrontation will last.
Béland said the deeper change probably will, partly because U.S. protectionism is likely to remain influential under future administrations.
“The idea that things will return to ‘normal’ once Donald Trump leaves the White House is probably just wishful thinking,” Béland said. “It doesn’t mean the relationship might not improve in the future but that things will never be the same.”

item.title: 日本领导人高市解释为何她长时间隐居官邸
item.description:
东京（美联社）——日本首相高市早苗周六表示，她更多地使用办公室旁边的官邸进行工作，以最大限度地提高效率。
12 月，高市搬进了官邸，这座砖石结构的宅邸于 1929 年启用，曾是原来的首相办公室，直到旁边建造了新的办公室。
高一在 X 上表示，住在官邸（或称“kotei”）很好，因为距离近，不需要通勤，可以让她在紧急情况下立即开始工作。
高一说，她加强了住所的办公功能，这样她就可以在需要时远程工作和开会，或者在需要时亲自与员工开会，即使是在办公时间之后。她还带家庭文件来阅读。
“对我来说，官邸也是一个工作场所，”她说。
但高市的工作口号以及她最近在 X 上透露的，由于除了担任首相的繁重工作之外，还要承担家务负担，晚上只能睡 0 到 3 个小时，引发了批评，认为这位日本第一位女性领导人在工作与生活平衡和性别平等方面树立了错误的榜样。
高市的支持率迅速下降，因为她推动了一些不受欢迎的政策，例如修改《皇室法》以加强男性继承制度，同时推迟采取经济措施来应对物价上涨。
媒体报道称，高市避开了议会会议，大部分时间在晚上和周末都躲在官邸里，并称她与其他议员和官员的互动和沟通比她的前任要少得多。Takaichi 经常在 X 上发表评论和政策，而不是与媒体交谈。
该官邸曾在 1930 年代发生过两次血腥政变，传说该建筑经常闹鬼。
尽管如此，高市显然并不介意在住所呆很长时间。
“我从来没有见过鬼，但我经常因为遇到蟑螂而尖叫，”她说。“当一只蟑螂从我脚边跑过时，我感到很震惊。”

item.title: 联邦法官撤销特朗普暂停处理 75 个国家移民签证的政策
item.description:
纽约一名联邦法官撤销了特朗普政府暂停处理来自 75 个国家签证的政策，其中包括阿富汗、伊朗、俄罗斯和索马里，特朗普政府认为这些国家的国民可能需要在美国提供公共援助。
前总统乔·拜登任命的美国地区法官珍妮特·巴尔加斯周五撤销了这项政策，称其“违反法律且超出法定权力”。
法官裁定，国务卿马可·卢比奥发布这项政策超越了他的职权，该政策要求“在没有任何法律依据的情况下拒绝向符合条件的申请人发放签证”，从而“违反”了《移民和国籍法》。
巴尔加斯表示，这项政策还破坏了国会将领事官员置于任何签证决定最前线的要求。
她写道：“国会赋予这些官员专属权力和自由裁量权，根据对法规中规定的具体和详细标准的审查来确定移民是否有资格获得签证。”“该政策明确禁止根据申请人的国籍签发移民签证，代表着对这一法定计划的直接废除。”
该政策受到两个非营利组织以及 11 个人的质疑，其中 6 人的家庭成员被拒绝签证。其余五人在国外，并已提交“基于就业的申请”来美国。
“我们欢迎这一裁决，因为从本质上讲，此案是为了让家庭团聚，”CLICNIC 的执行董事安娜·加拉格尔 (Anna Gallagher) 说。CLICNIC 是一家全国性非营利组织，为移民法律服务提供商网络提供培训、资源和支持，也是原告之一。
她在一份声明中说：“天主教的社会教义要求我们维护每个人的尊严，并承认家庭是社会的基础。”“这一决定肯定了这些价值观和法治，让家庭再次朝着团聚迈进。”
另一原告是位于哈莱姆区的非营利组织非洲社区。其一位领导人称这一裁决是“法治的巨大胜利”。
负责政策和宣传的副执行主任戴安娜·科纳特在一份声明中表示：“这项非法的种族主义禁令造成了不可估量的伤害，残酷地使家人和亲人分离。”“今天，我们很高兴地告诉我们的社区成员：这项禁令已不再存在。”
唐纳德·特朗普总统实施了越来越多的移民和旅行禁令，主要针对来自非洲、亚洲和拉丁美洲的人。美国国务院周六表示，特朗普政府正在“通过维护签证申请人的最高筛选和审查标准来保护美国人民”，并且不会对未决诉讼发表评论。
该政策发布时，国务院表示已指示领事官员停止来自 75 个国家的移民签证申请，这是根据 11 月份一项更广泛的命令，该命令收紧了对可能成为“公共负担”的潜在移民的规定。美国国务院根据经济顾问委员会的数据表示，超过 30% 的来自这些国家的移民家庭获得了某种形式的公共援助。
发给所有美国大使馆和领事馆的另一份通知称，非移民签证申请人也应接受“全面审查和筛选”，以确定他们可能在美国寻求公共福利的可能性。
美联社获得了该电报的副本，电报多次指出，申请人必须证明他们在美国期间不会申请公共福利，而怀疑申请人可能申请的领事官员应要求他们填写一份表格，证明其财务真实性。
该裁决是法院颠覆特朗普移民议程的最新例子。六月，一名联邦法官推翻了特朗普政府的一项政策，该政策使来自数十个国家的移民更难进入和留在美国，影响到庇护、工作许可、绿卡和公民身份申请等要素。该法官表示，这项政策使无数移民的生活“陷入不确定的法律困境”，并指责美国公民和移民服务局无视法律。

item.title: 随着风力增强，热带风暴莫克向夏威夷推进
item.description:
火奴鲁鲁（美联社）——热带风暴莫克周六向夏威夷推进，可能给大岛带来更多强降雨和强阵风，当地居民仍在应对飓风拉拉造成的严重洪水和破坏性大风的后果。
2026 年 8 月 17 日星期一，飓风拉拉带来大雨后，夏威夷纳阿莱胡的一条道路被泥土冲毁。（艾娜·阿卡姆，美联社）
莫克于周五在太平洋形成，位于希洛东南约 425 英里（680 公里）处，以 12 英里/小时（19 公里/小时）的速度向西北偏西移动。国家飓风中心表示，最大持续风速约为 50 英里/小时（85 公里/小时）。
与飓风拉拉一样，预计大岛将首当其冲地受到莫克降雨和强风的影响，因为它从周六晚间到周日早些时候直接袭击以南。
火奴鲁鲁国家气象局气象学家凯西·奥斯旺特表示，预计莫克将在周二早些时候继续在岛屿附近向西移动。
奥斯万特说：“影响仍然会存在，特别是对大岛的迎风面和东南面，但影响可能比我们在拉拉身上看到的要有限一些。”
拉拉砍倒了树木，将建筑物从地基上冲走，损坏了道路和桥梁，并使道路被泥土和岩石覆盖。据报道有两起与风暴有关的死亡事件。
2026 年 8 月 17 日星期一，夏威夷州纳阿勒胡飓风拉拉过后，Ka’u 汽车修理店被一片废墟包围。（Stephen Lam/《旧金山纪事报》，美联社）
奥斯万特说，预计大岛东南部和迎风面的周末降雨量为 5 至 10 英寸（13 至 25 厘米），偏远地区可达 15 英寸（38 厘米）。岛链其他地区预计降雨量为 1 至 2 英寸（2 至 5 厘米），但毛伊岛东部部分地区降雨量可能高达 4 英寸（10 厘米）。
目前没有有效的沿海监视或警告，但敦促人们密切监视风暴的进展。该中心表示，降雨有可能引发危险的离岸流、危及生命的洪水和泥石流，特别是在陡峭地区和地面仍然饱和的地方。
据气象部门称，大岛东北海岸的拉拉总降雨量最大，达 43.54 英寸（1.1 米）。据 poweroutage.us 称，夏威夷大岛仍有 8,000 多名客户断电。
2026 年 8 月 16 日星期日，在夏威夷山景城，恶劣天气系统袭击该地区后，一名青少年涉水穿过受损道路被冲毁的水池。（斯蒂芬·林 / 旧金山纪事报，美联社）
夏威夷州州长乔什·格林和其他州官员在莫克之前举行了新闻发布会，敦促人们做好准备，补充食品、药品和其他必需品。
住在大岛东侧凯奥的教师蒂芙尼·爱德华兹·亨特 (Tiffany Edwards Hunt) 表示，一想到社区里的降雨量增多，洪水变成了河流，“空气中肯定弥漫着紧张气氛”。
美联社底特律撰稿人亚历克斯·圣约翰对此作出了贡献。

item.title: 德克萨斯州法官驳回卡梅洛·安东尼就田径比赛致命刺伤案进行新审判的请求
item.description:
达拉斯（美联社）——周六，一名德克萨斯州法官驳回了对卡梅洛·安东尼在高中田径比赛中刺死一名 17 岁运动员的新审判，这一谋杀案引起了全国关注，并导致家属受到骚扰。
19 岁的安东尼于 6 月被判犯有谋杀罪，并因 2025 年 4 月杀害奥斯汀·梅特卡夫而被判处 35 年监禁。
本周在达拉斯附近举行为期两天的听证会后，迈克尔·奇蒂法官以对证据和论点的审查为由，以半页的命令驳回了重审动议。他没有详细说明。
安东尼的律师拉塞尔·威尔逊表示，辩方将上诉。
“我们对客户的承诺没有改变，”威尔逊说。“我们将继续通过一切合法途径大力为他辩护。”
安东尼重审请求的核心是检察官和他的审判辩护团队之间达成的一项非正式协议，以将有关这两名青少年的破坏性品格证据排除在诉讼之外。双方同意保留证据，以免进一步激化本已充满种族紧张局势和死亡威胁的案件。
该案引起了广泛关注，部分原因是大量社交媒体帖子以种族术语放大了这起杀戮事件。安东尼是黑人；梅特卡夫是白人。然而，双方律师都告诉陪审员，此案与种族无关。
安东尼的律师表示，担心检察官会在安东尼准备作证时违背协议，这是在双方律师发生激烈争执后发生的，并在最后一刻改变了辩护策略。安东尼最终决定不出庭作证。
检察官比尔·维尔斯基本周辩称审判是公平的。
科林县地方检察官格雷格·威利斯在宣布拒绝后表示：“我们尊重并期待法院拒绝重新审判动议的决定。”“陪审团的有罪判决成立，我们对这一过程仍然充满信心。每个被告都有权上诉，在上周听证会的痛苦经历中，我们的思念和祈祷仍然与梅特卡夫家族同在。”
安东尼的律师还要求重审，因为他们表示主审法官约翰·罗奇的法庭规则非常严格，限制了公众参与诉讼程序。在要求罗奇回避时，他们指出，罗奇接受了达拉斯一家电视台的审后采访，在采访中他表示同意陪审团的决定。
“无论他们说什么，他们都是对的，”罗奇说。
罗奇表示，他的规则对于公平审判是必要的，检察官坚称他没有做错任何事。
陪审员驳回了安东尼关于他在田径比赛看台上与梅特卡芬发生冲突时为自己辩护的说法。
安东尼和梅特卡夫是达拉斯郊区弗里斯科不同高中的运动员，比赛举行时的春日雨天，几支球队正在参加比赛。
目击者作证称，安东尼坐在梅特卡夫团队的帐篷下，梅特卡夫和其他人多次要求他离开。这导致对抗不断升级。
检察官称安东尼挑衅了梅特卡夫，目击者认定安东尼是侵略者。
据警方报告，安东尼有一次把手伸进一个袋子里说：“摸我，看看会发生什么。”
目击者称，梅特卡夫推了安东尼，安东尼掏出刀刺伤了他的胸部。

item.title: 特朗普翻修的白宫玫瑰园内部。首先是石头庭院，然后是雕像
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Instead of adding new roses, President Donald Trump’sWhite House Rose Gardenis growing statues.
Trump put statues of some of America’s founders in the garden just off the Oval Office after he replaced its plush lawn with awhite stone patio, turning the historic outdoor space into a look-alike of the one at his Mar-a-Lago home and private club in Palm Beach, Florida.
At least one statue was a gift. Others are on loan from people who wish to remain anonymous.
A statue of Alexander Hamilton is seen in the Rose Garden at the White House, March 6, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson, File)
The latest addition, a bronze depiction of a seated Thomas Jefferson signing the Declaration of Independence, was a gift from George Lundeen, a sculptor from Loveland, Colorado. It joins statues already displayed there of George Washington, Alexander Hamilton and Ben Franklin. A fifth sculpture named “Freedom’s Charge” is also on the patio.
The statues are part of Trump’s sweeping series ofWhite House renovations, from his gilded makeover of the Oval Office to theballroomandhelipadthat theRepublican presidentis having built on the south grounds. These projects fit into Trump’s broader plan to leave hismark on downtown Washingtonthrough otherconstruction projects, including astatue garden on federal landnear the National Mall.
Lundeen said he made the sculpture of Jefferson, the third U.S. president, decades ago and kept it at his ranch until he decided to spruce it up and send it to Trump for display at the White House in time for July Fourth celebrations ofAmerica’s 250th birthday. Steven Barber, his friend and collaborator, had reached out to contacts at the White House on Lundeen’s behalf.
“I thought it would just be a real nice thing on the 250th for people to look at Thomas Jefferson as he was writing the Declaration of Independence,” Lundeen said in a telephone interview.
But the statue did not get to the White House in time. Barber said it was stuck on a truck partly because of heavy security around the celebratory events. Trump was shown photos and liked the sculpture so much that he decided to put it in the Rose Garden.
When the president called Lundeen to thank him, he got voicemail. After the holiday, Lundeen’s office manager insisted he listen to one message in particular.

“Hi, George. It’s your favorite president, Donald Trump, and I just wanted to thank you,” the president said on the recording, which Lundeen shared with The Associated Press. “The sculpture, it looks really beautiful ... just by the picture I can see it’s really incredible, and we have a wonderful place right in the Rose Garden, and I appreciate it.”
Barber said in a separate telephone interview that he had been calling the White House for months to discuss the statue but got little in the way of a response until about three weeks before Independence Day, when in came a “flurry of emails saying they wanted it.”
A bronze statue of President George Washington is seen at the edge of the Rose Garden at the White House in Washington, Oct. 12, 2025. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein, File)
Details on the other statues added to the Rose Garden are relatively sparse.
The statue of Washington, America’s first president, was lent by Harlan Crow, the White House said. Representatives for the Texas-based real estate tycoon and GOP megadonor, who made headlines in recent years for hisfriendship with Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas, did not respond to email messages from the AP seeking comment.
A third statue, “Freedom’s Charge,” a 14-foot-tall (4.3-meter-tall) bronze sculpture of two Revolutionary War soldiers separated by a flag, was relocated from Dallas. Chas Fagan, the sculptor, did not respond to emailed requests for comment.
The Franklin and Hamilton statues are from anonymous donors, according to the White House.
White House spokesperson Davis Ingle explained Trump’s fondness for statues by saying that no other president has done more to beautify the White House and its surroundings.
“From restoring our treasured landmarks, which had suffered years of abuse and vandalism, to cleaning our parks and the Reflecting Pool, President Trump’s bold vision ensured that America rang in its 250th birthday celebration with glory and pride,” Ingle said in an emailed statement that referenced Trump’s troubled effort to spruce upthe pool near the Lincoln Memorial.
He said Trump continues to make “long-overdue and necessary” renovations to the White House.
“Thanks to the Builder-in-Chief, the White House will be properly glorified and remain in excellent condition for generations to come,” Ingle said.
President Donald Trump walks on the red carpet in the Rose Garden with Britain’s King Charles III, Queen Camilla and first lady Melania Trump at the White House, April 28, 2026, in Washington, during a State Visit. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon, File)
Next door to the White House, Trump had astatue of Christopher Columbus installedon the grounds of the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in March.
More recently, the National Park Service installed a series of sculptures of Revolutionary-era subjects and themes at a plaza near the White House.
Trump’s marquee statue plan involves building aNational Garden of American Heroesnear the National Mall that would feature sculptures of 250 Americans who have made significant cultural, political and other historical contributions to the United States. Several preservation and cultural heritage organization have sued to block the project, arguing that Congress must first authorize it.
Barber said he and Lundeen are “in the mix” to make statues for that garden, too.
At his golf club in West Palm Beach, Florida, Trump has on display a 7-foot (2.1-meter) bronze sculpture depicting him with his fist raised after the 2024 assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. It was also made by Lundeen and was given to Trump by Anthony Constantino, a businessman and Republican congressional candidate from New York.
A statue of Ben Franklin is seen as servers prepare the Rose Garden for a dinner after President Donald Trump hosted the 2026 College Football Playoff national champions Indiana University on the South Lawn of the White House, May 11, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin, File)
The White House has long been a showcase for art, perhaps no work more famous than the Gilbert Stuart portrait of Washington that hangs in the East Room and was saved by first lady Dolly Madison after the British set the White House on fire during the War of 1812.
Presidents have access to the White House’s vast art collection. Trump has said he went to the “vaults” and found the presidential portraits and other art he hung in the Oval Office and in other rooms in the White House. Portraits of former presidents and former first ladies also adorn hallways and public rooms in the mansion.
In Trump’s first term, first lady Melania Trump installeda piece by Japanese American sculptor Isamu Noguchinear the Rose Garden, making him the first Asian American artist to be featured in the White House collection.
Before that, then-first lady Michelle Obama’s renovation of the Old Family Dining Room in 2015 included the addition of a painting by Alma Thomas, who was the first African American female artist to have her work added to the collection.

item.title: 特朗普敦促法院驳回BBC在诽谤案中获取其家人记录的请求
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——唐纳德·特朗普总统敦促联邦法官驳回 BBC 请求法院帮助获取三名家庭成员的证词和文件的请求，以回应他针对英国广播公司提起的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤诉讼。
这位共和党总统的私人律师在周五的法庭文件中辩称，BBC 正试图通过向女儿伊万卡·特朗普、女婿贾里德·库什纳和儿子小唐纳德·特朗普发出传票来获得对特朗普的“政治影响力”。
迈阿密的美国地区法官杰弗里·昆茨没有立即对这一纠纷做出裁决。
被特朗普提名为法官的昆茨不到一周前从另一位法官手中继承了总统的诉讼。法院文件没有立即具体说明案件重新分配的原因。前任法官已定下二月的审判日期。
据总统的律师称，今年 5 月，一名为 BBC 工作的传票员试图在伊万卡·特朗普和库什纳的住所向他们送达传票，但遇到了特勤局特工，特勤局特工表示他们无权接受传票。他们表示，几天后，流程服务器还访问了纽约的特朗普大厦，但未能为小唐纳德·特朗普提供服务。
在上周提交的法庭文件中，该广播公司请求法院允许通过挂号信而不是亲自向特朗普的家人送达传票。
特朗普于 12 月提起诉讼，指控 BBC 对他 2021 年 1 月 6 日在白宫附近发表的演讲的部分内容进行了欺骗性编辑，当时特朗普的一群支持者袭击了国会大厦，以阻止国会认可民主党人乔·拜登战胜特朗普。该诉讼称，BBC 将特朗普演讲的不同部分拼接在一起，故意歪曲他的言论。
该诉讼称，BBC 在 2024 年总统大选前一周播出了这部纪录片，“公然试图干涉和影响”选举结果，损害特朗普的利益。
特朗普的律师写道：“BBC 动议所寻求的救济不能与该动议所基于的充满政治色彩的发现运动分开，该运动已被本法院裁定为不当过于宽泛。”

BBC 已就误导性编辑向特朗普道歉，但否认诽谤他。

item.title: 特朗普希望中期选举是关于他自己的。这对于罕见的内布拉斯加州摇摆区可能没有帮助
item.description:
OMAHA, Neb. (AP) — “Do they still like Trump in Nebraska? I think so,” the president said during a recent event in Washington.
Given that the state easily backed RepublicanDonald Trumpthree times and hasn’t supported a Democrat for the White House since Lyndon B. Johnson in 1964, the answer may seem obvious.
But in Nebraska’s largest city, it’s an open question and could decide one of the country’s most-watched congressional races. Retiring Rep.Don Bacon’s open seat pits fellow Republican and Omaha City CouncilmemberBrinker Hardingagainst Democratic activistDenise Powell.
The district encompasses an increasingly Democratic-leaning Omaha metro area of 1 million-plus and its more conservative suburbs — famous for steaks and the Reuben sandwich’s birthplace, though New York disputes that.
It’s one of just eight districts nationwide that elected Republicans in House races while supporting Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris over Trump two years ago.
Harding and Powell have been making the rounds at parades and festivals where meat raffles offer oversized sausages as prizes. However, those on-the-ground appeals could be drowned out by Trump who, like most things in politics, has moved to shape November’smidterm electionsinhis own image.
The president is organizing aRepublican midterm convention in Dallasnext month that will serve as much a two-day rally for him as a boon to party candidates nationwide. Trump is also frequently visiting tightly contested districts, despite hislow approval ratingsand theunpopular war in Iran.
While Trump centers himself, Democrats are happy to oblige.
When Powell knocks on doors to talk to voters, she asks, “What’s keeping you up at night?” On a sweaty Saturday afternoon, John Rosseter responded without hesitation. “Well, Trump.”
“I want to see the history books written years from now,” said Rosseter, 67, who owns a carpentry business. “They won’t be pretty.”

Nebraska splits its presidential electoral votes, and the 2nd Congressional District’s delegate has gone to Democrats three out of five times since 2008, making it a “blue dot” in an otherwise Republican red state. But a Democrat has won the House seat just once since 1994.
Harding plays up Trump’s primary endorsement, and House SpeakerMike Johnsonand Majority LeaderSteve Scalisecampaigned for him. Harding said he has “the full confidence of, not only the White House, but leadership in the Congress.”
He has also tried to appeal to swing voters and says he knows the district better than does Powell, co-founder of Women Who Run Nebraska, which supports female candidates.
Two possible Democratic 2028 presidential candidates — ex-Transportation SecretaryPete ButtigiegandRahm Emanuel, an ex-Chicago mayor who was President Barack Obama’s first White House chief of staff — have campaigned with Powell.
She talks about howMedicare cutshave increasedanxiety about affordability. Powell also points to Trump and his family’sbusiness dealingsas an example of “the choices that they have made while people on the ground are struggling” and she says that resonates with Republicans.
“Even the ones who aren’t necessarily anti-Trump,” Powell said, “understand the need for checks and balances.”
Jason Brown and his wife, Ruth Huebner-Brown, caused a sensation in 2024 by spray painting about 50 reused lawn signs with blue dots and distributing them around Omaha’s Dundee neighborhood. The couple has since expanded to professionally produce signs promoting a “Blue Dot Wave.”
Brown said the Republican-controlled Congress has capitulated on “every Trump nominee, every Trump policy, all the way down to putting gilding gold on statues.”
Supporters of Harding have countered with red “Brinker Dot” signs.
“We need to make sure that we keep this country on the track to being even better,” Harding said.
Jack Hosking, the 90-year-old retired former head of a title insurance company, organizes a weekly coffee to discuss political and community issues. He estimated that about 70% of attendees are Trump voters and “maybe even more so lately, because of the crap that the New York mayor started,” referring to Zohran Mamdani’s efforts at pushing the Democratic Party to the left.
Both Powell and Harding have addressed Hosking’s group, though, and he predicted that as much as half will support the Democrat.
“She spoke well enough that, my sense is, a lot of them will cross over,” Hosking said, noting that when it came to campaigning, “Brinker’s not doing much.”
The Republican National Committee views Trump as a national asset, betting he can prevent complacency in a year without a presidential race, when enthusiasm for the party in powertypically wanes.
The committee rebranded its “Young Guns” program for key candidates to “MAGA Majority” in deference to Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement, and many congressional candidates will be at the Dallas convention with Trump.
Republican Reps.Mike Lawlerof New York andTom Barrettof Michigan, whom Democrats are aiming to unseat, both appeared with Trump during his rallies in their districts. When the presidentvisitedMacungie, Pennsylvania, in June, he joined Republican Rep. Ryan Mackenzie, saying, “I’m here for him.”
Trump also traveled to the Wisconsin district of Republican Rep. Derreck Van Orden, as have Cabinet members.
Rep. Juan Ciscomani, facing a reelection fight, appeared with Trump during an April event in Arizona. Two Iowa Republicans in what could be toss-up reelection contests, Reps Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks, both were by Trump’s side when hekicked off his midterm campaignoutside Des Moines.
Bacon sometimes defied the White House in his final term. He criticized Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and tried to curb Trump’s ability toimpose tariffsand was the only House Republican who opposedrenaming the Gulf of Mexicoas the Gulf of America.
Mary Jane Truemper, who heads the Nebraska Republican Party, said Powell and the state’s Democrats have moved too far to the left. She called Harding “a steady force” and said the nominee is not as fond of picking high-profile fights the way Bacon sometimes was.
“I think he speaks to the moderate Democrats as well as the Republicans,” said Truemper, who managed Bacon’s reelection campaign in 2018 and also worked for an unsuccessful primary challenger to him.
Even Powell said, “Don Bacon was a good representative of this district, and I think that there are a lot of people drawn to a pragmatic style of leadership in a state like ours.” But that may not be enough this year.
“People are worse off than they were before,” Powell said.
In the Elmwood Park neighborhood, Andy Maxwell, a 58-year-old pediatrician, said he likes to find the middle ground in politics and his community. But he recalled that, after putting up a Biden sign in his yard in 2020, his neighbors erected a Trump one.
“We don’t like all the turmoil part of it,” Maxwell said of politics nationally.
Nearby, 80-year-old Jerard Pearson called Democrats “feckless,” but said of Trump’s base supporters, “I’ve always been curious about this one-third level of crazy out there, a third of the population.” He is also no fan of a neighbor’s large “Harding for Congress” sign.
Truemper said Harding appreciates Trump’s endorsement but Nebraskans like to be wooed “person-to-person, rather than a national entity coming in.”
“Is that going to be the deciding factor?” she asked of Trump. “I don’t know.”

item.title: 跨性别辩论在 Fever 比赛中引发集会，布里安娜·斯图尔特 (Breanna Stewart) 希望有一个安全的空间
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——纽约自由队球星布里安娜·斯图尔特一直将 WNBA 视为一个包容性的地方，为球迷和球员提供安全的空间。最近这一点受到了挑战。
最近，WNBA 一直是关于是否应该允许跨性别女性（出生时被指定为男性，但为了适应自己的性别认同而转变）的辩论的主题。WNBA从来没有出现过这样的球员。尽管联盟的集体谈判协议规定 WNBA 仅限女性参加，但它没有包含有关性别认同或出生性别的更具体的语言。
印第安纳狂热队的索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 在上个月发布的 ESPN 简介中表示，她反对变性女孩和妇女参加女子和女子运动项目，此后，印第安纳狂热队的索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 表示，她反对跨性别女孩和妇女参加女子和女子运动项目，这一问题达到了紧要关头，随后，印第安纳狂热队比赛场外出现了小型集会和抗议活动。在周六晚上狂热队对阵纽约自由队之前，举行了两次代表跨性别问题双方的和平集会。
周六上午，斯图尔特对一小​​群记者表示：“知道双方都在举行集会，这表明W党拥有的平台和吸引注意力的噱头只是在继续尝试驾驭我们现有的浪潮。”“我希望今晚来到这里的自由球迷甚至印地球迷能够让这个竞技场成为一个安全的空间。”
坎宁安认为，她的评论所吸引的所有关注都是积极的，因为它为比赛带来了更多粉丝。
“你有很多新球迷，他们不仅会观看比赛，还会来看比赛，看看环境，看看人才，”她在赛前说道。“我认为任何时候你都能吸引更多人关注 W，这是一件很棒的事情，因为这会激励其他可能从未见过这款游戏、听说过这款游戏或参加过游戏的孩子，他们会获得这种体验。所以我绝对认为这是一件非常积极的事情。”
上周日在亚特兰大梦想队和狂热队之间的比赛中，至少三名球迷被 WNBA 安保人员要求遮盖印有变性女性参与女子运动的信息的衬衫。联盟后来表示球迷应该可以自由穿着这些球衣。
斯图尔特特别表示，自由球迷和 WNBA 球迷都会来观看比赛，因为“他们会觉得自己可以以任何身份做自己，我们不想忽视这一点。”
这位自由前锋表示，每个人都有权发表自己的意见，如果这种情况不再被允许，就会出现更大的问题。然而，她表示，不应容忍试图分裂球队和球员的行为。
“如果我们不允许（言论自由），我们需要真正回去看看更多的事情。我认为更重要的是人们试图将我们划分为团队、队友或对手，”她说。“这个联盟具有令人难以置信的包容性，也是我们继续争取和反对的目标。因此，我们不想剥夺这个平台。”
斯图尔特在她的职业生涯中一直是跨性别群体的盟友。去年，当她的一款签名鞋带有哈利波特主题时，她在网上遭到了一些强烈反对。斯图尔特是《哈利·波特》系列书籍和作者 J.K. 的后续电影的超级粉丝。罗琳斯因其反变性而受到批评。
斯图尔特已将该鞋的版税捐赠给了 Trevor Project，这是一个针对 LGBTQ+ 青少年的自杀预防和危机干预非营利组织。

item.title: 因凡蒂诺无视国际足联副主席的邀请，在全球足球裂痕中前往加勒比海举办青少年活动
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——詹尼·因凡蒂诺（Gianni Infantino）无视国际足联一位副主席提出的远离加勒比海地区 14 岁以下足球赛事的要求，而是罕见地在全球因他将未来世界杯利润出售给私人投资者的计划失败而引起轩然大波时公开露面。
周六，因凡蒂诺在他的 Instagram 帐户上发布了照片，照片显示国际足联主席在蓬塔卡纳度假胜地举行的加勒比足球联盟 (CFU) 青年锦标赛期间会见了多米尼加共和国的政治和足球官员。
周五，总部位于迈阿密的大陆足球组织中北美洲及加勒比海足球协会(CONCACAF)加拿大主席维克多·蒙塔利亚尼(Victor Montagliani)要求因凡蒂诺不要前往，以免影响足球比赛。
蒙塔利亚尼在美联社看到的一封电子邮件信中写道：“我相信，考虑到由于你们有争议的国际足联前进企业提案而引发的围绕国际足联的治理危机，媒体将关注这种情况，”蒙塔利亚尼在美联社看到的一封电子邮件信中写道，“不幸的是，这将大大削弱 CFU 青年竞赛的技术性质。”
蒙塔利亚尼写道：“因此，我以足球的名义恭请您重新考虑您的出席，因为这将不幸地破坏这项重要的青年发展活动的技术性质。”
国际足联拒绝对蒙塔利亚尼的请求发表评论，但指出国际足联从每四年的世界杯周期中直接资助 CFU 等地区机构最多 500 万美元。
蒙塔利亚尼与国际足联副主席、欧洲机构欧足联的亚历山大·塞弗林以及亚洲足球联合会主席谢赫·萨勒曼·本·易卜拉欣·阿勒哈利法结盟，寻求结束因凡蒂诺在第11个年头日益担任主席职务。
他们两周前指责因凡蒂诺在过去一年里秘密计划将国际足联价值数十亿美元的商业活动剥离给约书亚·库什纳领导的投资者持有20%股份的子公司，这是“欺骗”。
由于全球足球领袖和球迷的强烈反对，因凡蒂诺于 8 月 1 日撤回了该项目，几个小时前，他自己的首席运营官在给美联社的一份声明中对该提案及其领导风格发表了严厉批评。苏黎世首席运营官凯文·拉穆尔 (Kevin Lamour) 本周被解雇。
加勒比海地区的会员联合会被视为因凡蒂诺脱离中北美洲及加勒比海足联领导权的潜在支持者。南美足协支持因凡蒂诺作为举办 2030 年世界杯更多比赛的最佳途径，并希望将参赛球队从 48 支球队扩大到 64 支球队。
自英国日报《泰晤士报》7 月 28 日披露耗资 200 亿美元的 FFE 项目以来，国际足联领导人一直没有公开接受质询，周五在蓬塔卡纳对英国广播公司天空新闻的记者提出了质疑。
当天空记者詹姆斯·马修斯问他是否背叛了这项运动并应该辞职时，因凡蒂诺说“非常感谢”，并嘲笑两人都是秃头。
因凡蒂诺的目标是在明年 3 月于摩洛哥拉巴特举行的国际足联选举大会上再次当选，第四次也是最后一次任期到 2031 年。国际足联已将 11 月 18 日定为潜在候选人参加竞选的最后期限。

item.title: 老鹰队的贾昆登·杰克逊受伤后被救护车送下场，现在还能活动
item.description:
马萨诸塞州福克斯伯勒（美联社）——费城老鹰队跑卫贾昆登·杰克逊在周六晚上对阵新英格兰爱国者队的季前赛开球时受伤，被救护车带离球场。
老鹰队宣布杰克逊四肢仍有力量和活动能力，已被送往医院接受进一步评估。
杰克逊是开球队的一员，他对新英格兰队的兰·拉里森进行了铲球，但比赛结束后几秒钟就一动不动了。
当两支球队的医务人员都在照顾杰克逊时，训练员们几乎立即赶了过来。他们很快叫来了篮板和救护车。
当他被绑在担架上时，两支球队的球员都跪在边线附近。在杰克逊被送上救护车之前，老鹰队的球员短暂包围了他。可以看到杰克逊短暂地举起左臂。
替补四分卫坦纳·麦基赛后表示，他们在赛后被告知杰克逊没事。
“有很多不同的情绪，只是祈祷并希望他没事，”麦基说。“有传言说他在说话，他反应灵敏并且移动。这让每个人都平静下来，我们知道我们的队友做得很好。”

item.title: 摩城早期歌曲作家珍妮·布拉德福德·霍布斯 (Janie Bradford Hobbs) 因病在洛杉矶去世，享年 87 岁
item.description:
摩城早期歌曲作家珍妮·布拉德福德·霍布斯 (Janie Bradford Hobbs) 的家人周六表示，她因长期患病在洛杉矶一家医院去世，她曾帮助创作了《Money (That's What I Want)》和《Too Busy Thinking About My Baby》等热门歌曲。她87岁了。
布拉德福德·霍布斯出生于密苏里州查尔斯顿，后来搬到底特律。
20 世纪 50 年代末，她经邻居兼歌手杰基·威尔逊 (Jackie Wilson) 介绍认识了摩城创始人贝里·戈迪 (Berry Gordy)。她于 1958 年加入摩城担任接待员，与公司的许多员工一样，她参与了创意过程，帮助摩城成为音乐行业的巨头。
她和戈迪合写了《金钱（这就是我想要的）》。这首歌由 Barrett Strong 于 1959 年录制，并成为早期热门歌曲。它被披头士乐队翻唱，也成为该乐队的热门歌曲之一。
《Too Busy Thinking About My Baby》首先由 The Temptations 录制，后来成为马文·盖伊 (Marvin Gaye) 的热门歌曲。布拉德福德·霍布斯还为史蒂夫·旺德、The Supremes、Martha & The Vandellas 等人创作了歌曲。
戈迪在一份声明中说：“珍妮从一开始就和我在一起，甚至在摩城还没有出现之前，她将永远在我心中和摩城大家庭中占据一个非常特殊的位置。”
“珍妮是我一直认为摩城家族的特殊群体之一，他们是无名英雄，在人们知道摩城会变成什么样子之前，他们就相信了自己的梦想，”戈迪继续说道。“她是帮助摩城发展成为现在这个样子的人之一。”
布拉德福德·霍布斯后来成为摩城出版公司乔贝特的作家关系主管。离开摩城后，她创办了年度英雄与传奇奖。据她的家人称，这项活动持续了大约 30 年，旨在表彰音乐偶像并颁发奖学金。
她的丈夫沃丁·霍布斯（Wardean Hobbs）去世了。女儿，妮可·霍布斯；儿子，兰斯·芬尼；和两个孙子。葬礼尚未完成。

item.title: Journey 正在为摇滚乐队最后一次巡演的最后一站做准备
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——漫长的骑行之路再次向标志性摇滚乐队 Journey 的成员们招手。这是乐队最后的旅程吗？
他们的告别巡演的最后一站将于 9 月在洛杉矶拉开序幕，最后的旅程可能会在 11 月的旧金山结束，这将是一场充满情感的回家之旅。
“我确信这会有些情绪化，因为这就是一切的开始，”联合创始人兼主音吉他手尼尔·舍恩说。“我知道观众会摆脱困境。”
在决赛之前，乐队还有很多演出，包括凤凰城、西雅图、芝加哥、亚特兰大、纳什维尔、巴尔的摩、费城、底特律、波士顿、克利夫兰、丹佛和拉斯维加斯等地。
今年巡演在旧金山的最后一场演出将为 100 多场音乐会画上圆满句号，乐队经常演奏两个多小时，并加入深度剪辑——比如 70 年代初的空旷、旋律优美的“Of a Lifetime”和 80 年代专辑“Raising on Radio”中的歌曲——以及可靠的热门歌曲，如“Faithously”。
“我很喜欢它，因为这就是我一直想用 Journey 制作的演出类型，”Schon 说道。当该乐队与 REO Speedwagon、Styx 或foreigner 等其他 80 年代乐队混为一谈时，他感到很沮丧。
“我总觉得，尽管所有这些乐队都贡献了很多人喜欢的东西，但我们还是很不同。我认为在音乐上我们可以去任何我们想去的地方。所以现在我们终于这么做了。”
《Journey》有 6 张专辑进入 Billboard 单曲榜前 10 名，其中包括《Open Arms》和《Who’s Crying Now》，还有 8 张专辑进入 Billboard 200 排行榜前 10 名，其中包括 1981 年排名第一的《Escape》。
粉丝们可以期待听到这些热门歌曲以及《Journey》经久不衰的主题曲“Don’t Stop Believin”，这是 Schon 与键盘手 Jonathan Cain 和当时的主唱 Steve Perry 共同创作的歌曲。
它曾出现在百老汇剧目《Rock of Ages》、《黑道家族》的黑人结局、电视节目《欢乐合唱团》、布拉德·皮特的《点球成金》、电影《怪物》和 2024 年民主党全国代表大会点名中。在经历了一个夏天，在世界杯上听到《Don’t Stop Believin’》以及纽约尼克斯队赢得 NBA 冠军之后，今年秋天，《Journey》将重返公路。
“《Don’t Stop Believin》超出了我们的预期，”凯恩说。“每个乐队都希望自己有一张，我们也有一张。所以，我想这就是我们的‘Hey Jude’名片。所以我们会接受它。”
除了 Schon 和 Cain 之外，目前的 Journey 阵容还包括歌手 Arnel Pineda、键盘手 Jason Derlatka、鼓手 Deen Castronovo 和贝斯手 Todd Jensen。凯恩、德拉特卡和卡斯特罗诺沃拿起麦克风，让皮内达在一些歌曲上休息一下。
乐队成员说，他们放眼望去，发现有五代人参加他们的演出。“我喜欢说《旅程》是不确定时期的特定音乐，”凯恩说。“旅程是很多人生活的配乐。”
舍恩（左）和史蒂夫·佩里出席 2017 年摇滚名人堂入职典礼。（查尔斯·赛克斯/Invision/美联社拍摄，档案）
这支乐队在黑胶唱片时代诞生于旧金山，经历了音乐行业的巨大变革——CD、Napster、数字和流媒体。舍恩 (Schon) 与卡洛斯·桑塔纳 (Carlos Santana) 一起演奏初露锋芒，他还记得《旅程》早期为 Kiss、Jeff Beck 和 Cheech and Chong 开场的情景。
巡演似乎是大多数乐队赚钱的唯一途径，因为每首流媒体歌曲只能赚到一小部分钱。Journey 偏向于旅游，有时一日游三座城市。
“我为新一代感到难过，”凯恩说。“我记得当我收到一张又大又旧的版税支票时，他们在广播中播放我们的歌曲，一张新专辑意味着你会卖出更多的门票。今天不是这样。”
终点——11 月 28 日在大通中心——即将到来，但乐队不确定当晚会包括什么。“到此结束肯定是合适的，”凯恩说。“谁知道谁会出现？我不知道。我希望，可能会有某种团聚。”
之后，乐队就不确定了。凯恩表示：“未来的前景确实还悬而未决。”舍恩同意这一观点，但尚未准备好做出预测。
“我想做的事情还没有完成，”他说。“我认为未来会有很多很好的机会。无论现在在座的每个人是否都拥有这样的机会，我都不确定。”
